subject: Reasoning
topic: Classification — Odd One Out Across Numbers, Letters, Science and Language (W12 B1)

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Apple, Banana, Cherry, Carrot
questions.explanation: D is correct. Apple, Banana and Cherry are fruits. Carrot is a vegetable (root vegetable). The odd one out based on the category FRUIT. Trap: one might argue Cherry is different from the others in some way — but all three (apple, banana, cherry) are fleshy fruits eaten as snacks, while carrot belongs to a different food category entirely.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Dog, Cat, Cow, Eagle
questions.explanation: D is correct. Dog, Cat and Cow are mammals (warm-blooded, give birth to live young, nurse with milk). Eagle is a bird (feathers, lays eggs, hollow bones). The classification is based on the biological class: mammals vs. birds. Trap: all four are animals, so the level of grouping must be finer — specifically MAMMALS vs NON-MAMMAL.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? 2, 4, 6, 9
questions.explanation: D is correct. 2, 4 and 6 are even numbers. 9 is an odd number. The odd one out is 9. Also: 2, 4, 6 are consecutive even numbers; 9 doesn't fit. Trap: one might argue 2 is prime and 4,6 are composite and 9 is composite — but this grouping would make 2 the odd one out, which is not the most prominent/obvious classification. Even/odd is the primary pattern.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Violin, Guitar, Sitar, Flute
questions.explanation: D is correct. Violin, Guitar and Sitar are STRING instruments (produce sound by vibrating strings, either plucked or bowed). Flute is a WIND instrument (produces sound by the player blowing air through/across a hole). Classification: type of musical instrument. Trap: one might note that violin uses a bow while guitar/sitar are plucked — but all three are still string instruments, whereas flute is categorically different (wind).

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? 144, 169, 196, 198
questions.explanation: D is correct. 144=12², 169=13², 196=14² — all are perfect squares. 198 is not a perfect square (√198≈14.07). The odd one out is 198. Verify: 14²=196, 15²=225; there is no integer n such that n²=198. Trap: some students might check if they are perfect cubes or have other properties — but perfect square is the most obvious shared property among 144, 169 and 196.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon
questions.explanation: D is correct. Mercury, Venus and Earth are planets that orbit the Sun. The Moon is a natural satellite that orbits Earth (not the Sun directly). Classification: planets vs. natural satellite. Trap: all four are celestial bodies (too broad a category to reveal the odd one out); the specific distinction is PLANET (orbits star) vs SATELLITE (orbits planet).

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? ABCD, FGHIJ, LMNO, PQRS
questions.explanation: B is correct. ABCD has 4 letters (A,B,C,D — consecutive). LMNO has 4 letters (consecutive). PQRS has 4 letters (consecutive). FGHIJ has 5 letters (F,G,H,I,J — consecutive). The odd one out is FGHIJ (has 5 letters, not 4 like the rest). All groups contain consecutive alphabetic letters; only FGHIJ has a different count. Trap: students might look for a different pattern (e.g., vowels, starting letter pattern) — count of letters is the primary distinguishing feature.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Square, Rectangle, Rhombus, Kite
questions.explanation: D is correct. Square, Rectangle and Rhombus are all PARALLELOGRAMS — quadrilaterals where both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. A Kite is NOT a parallelogram — in a kite, adjacent sides are equal (two pairs), but opposite sides are not parallel. The odd one out is Kite. Trap: all four are quadrilaterals (4-sided figures) — too broad; the relevant distinction is specifically PARALLELOGRAM vs NON-PARALLELOGRAM.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
questions.explanation: D is correct. 8=2³, 27=3³, 64=4³, 125=5³ — all are perfect cubes. 100=10² is a perfect SQUARE but NOT a perfect cube (∛100≈4.64). The odd one out is 100. Trap: 64=2⁶=4³ is both a perfect cube and a perfect square — but it IS a perfect cube, so it belongs with the group. 100 is not a perfect cube at all. Trap: students who focus on 100 being 'a round number' may miss the perfect cube property.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? 49, 56, 63, 72, 77
questions.explanation: D is correct. 49=7×7, 56=7×8, 63=7×9, 77=7×11 — all are multiples of 7. 72=8×9=72; 72÷7=10.28... (not an integer) — 72 is NOT a multiple of 7. The odd one out is 72. Verify: 49÷7=7 ✓; 56÷7=8 ✓; 63÷7=9 ✓; 77÷7=11 ✓; 72÷7=10.28... ✗. Trap: all numbers look close in value (49–77); only careful checking of divisibility by 7 reveals 72 as the outlier. Note: 125 was the last option (D) = 77, not 125 — the question shows options A)49, B)56, C)63, D)72.
